paper.title: SkillRL: Evolving Agents via Recursive Skill-Augmented Reinforcement Learning
paper.central_claim: Distilling raw trajectories into a hierarchical SkillBank (general + task-specific skills), teaching the policy to use it via cold-start SFT, and recursively evolving the library from validation failures during GRPO yields higher ALFWorld/WebShop/search-QA performance than raw-memory and memory-augmented RL baselines.

evidence.quote: Existing memory-based methods primarily store raw trajectories, which are often redundant and noise-heavy.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: raw-trajectory memory is verbose/noisy; the fixed object replaced is the trajectory store.

evidence.quote: a recursive evolution mechanism that allows the skill library to co-evolve with the agent’s policy during reinforcement learning
evidence.support_explanation: Central retained-object claim: a skill library revised during RL.

evidence.quote: Unlike prior approaches that retain only successful episodes, we deliberately preserve both successful trajectories
evidence.support_explanation: Distillation consumes successes and failures with differential processing (teacher abstraction vs failure-lesson synthesis).

evidence.quote: direct inclusion in context is infeasible due to their length and noise. Instead, we synthesize concise failure lessons:
evidence.support_explanation: Failures are turned into 4-part counterfactual lessons by the teacher rather than stored raw.

evidence.quote: Task-specific skills are retrieved via semantic similarity:
evidence.support_explanation: Read path: embedding top-K with similarity threshold; general skills always included (next evidence).

evidence.quote: are always included as foundational guidance.
evidence.support_explanation: General skills are unconditionally injected, so the executor always reads them.

evidence.quote: Simply providing skills to an unchanged model yields limited benefit
evidence.support_explanation: Motivation for teacher-generated cold-start SFT; the policy must be taught to use skills.

evidence.quote: After each validation epoch, we monitor the success rate
evidence.support_explanation: Evolution trigger uses per-category validation success; the data feeding evolution is validation-set failures.

evidence.quote: The teacher model is prompted to: (1) identify failure patterns not addressed by current skills, (2) propose new skills to cover these gaps, and (3) suggest refinements to existing skills that proved ineffective.
evidence.support_explanation: Candidate generation for library edits is a teacher prompt; no execution test, held-out check or rollback of proposed skills is described; how "proved ineffective" is determined is unspecified.

evidence.quote: as the teacher model for skill distillation and SFT data generation.
evidence.support_explanation: OpenAI o3 is the teacher for both skill distillation and cold-start SFT traces (external stronger model in the loop).

evidence.quote: the 12.3% absolute improvement over GRPO on ALFWorld (from 77.6% to 89.9%) is directly attributable to our skill-augmentation mechanism rather than algorithmic variance.
evidence.support_explanation: Author causal claim; contradicted in scope by the pipeline also adding o3 cold-start SFT and distillation (see E015, E019) and by absent seeds.
Vanilla GRPO (no SFT, no skills): ALFWorld All 77.6, WebShop score 79.3 / success 66.1; the star marks a number replicated from another paper (E035).

evidence.quote: ∗ denotes the results replicated from [ 8 ] .
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline numbers (including GRPO, RLOO, ReAct) are taken from another paper rather than re-run under this pipeline, so training budget/protocol parity is unverified.

evidence.quote: Max new skills per evolution 3
evidence.support_explanation: Each evolution event can add at most 3 skills; with a 5-step interval this bounds growth (observed 55 -> 100).
SkillRL: ALFWorld All 89.9, WebShop score 85.2 / success 72.7.

evidence.quote: w/o Hier. 76.8 61.4 w/o Skill Lib. 61.7 50.2
evidence.support_explanation: Removing hierarchy: 76.8/61.4; replacing the library with raw trajectories: 61.7/50.2 (full 89.9/72.7).
Without cold-start SFT 65.2/46.5; with a static library (no dynamic evolution) 84.4/70.3.

evidence.quote: Dynamic evolution contributes a 5.5% improvement by ensuring the skill library is a dynamic component rather than a static database.
evidence.support_explanation: Evolution effect size: +5.5 ALFWorld (89.9 vs 84.4) and +2.4 WebShop (72.7 vs 70.3), single run, measured on the split that drives evolution.

evidence.quote: Cold-start SFT proves critical (20% drop without it)
evidence.support_explanation: Teacher-demonstration SFT is the largest single dependency besides the library.

evidence.quote: The Qwen2.5-7B model falls below the capability threshold required to simultaneously navigate complex environments and abstract high-quality skills.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors concede self-distillation fails at 7B; o3 teacher supplies the abstraction.

evidence.quote: Qwen2.5-7B Base model 14.8 7.8 15.2 SkillRL (policy model) 42.5 19.6 35.7 SkillRL (o3) 89.9 72.7 47.1
evidence.support_explanation: With the policy model itself distilling skills the 7B reaches only 42.5/19.6 (ALFWorld/WebShop), far below GRPO 77.6/66.1; the headline needs o3.

evidence.quote: Kimi-K2.5 successfully distills skills from its own trial-and-error experience, significantly boosting its own performance (e.g., 71.2 to 88.5 on ALFWorld, 45.9 to 73.4 on WebShop) entirely without the o3 teacher.
evidence.support_explanation: For a 1.1T model, self-distilled skill pipeline improves over its own base, a retained-library gain without external teacher (author-reported, no baseline pipeline control).

evidence.quote: Success rate on ALFWorld validation set.
evidence.support_explanation: Learning curves and the evolution ablation are on a "validation set"; the evolution failures also come from validation epochs; the split behind Table 1 is not stated.

evidence.quote: Through dynamic evolution, this grows to 100 skills by the end of training (Step 150).
evidence.support_explanation: Library grows 55 -> 100 skills (12->20 general, 43->80 task-specific); no pruning/retirement is reported.

evidence.quote: Total wall-clock time: approximately 30 hours per experiment.
evidence.support_explanation: Compute reported for the proposed method on 8xH100 (collection 3h, distillation 0.5h, SFT 2h, RL 24h); no matched-budget baselines, no o3 API volume/cost.

evidence.quote: currently relies on a high-capability teacher model for the critical skill distillation and synthetic trajectory generation phases.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors state teacher dependence and unresolved SkillBank-scale retrieval noise.

evidence.quote: Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [No]
evidence.support_explanation: Authors answer No for error bars/significance; no seeds, denominators or CIs are given for ALFWorld/WebShop.

evidence.quote: achieving approximately a 10.3% reduction in context length.
evidence.support_explanation: Prompt-length saving vs raw-memory baseline is about 10% (1,300 vs 1,450 tokens), smaller than the introduction suggests.

evidence.quote: MemRL, which uses RL solely to update its memory bank while keeping the policy frozen, fails to adapt to complex environments, yielding only 21.4% on ALFWorld.
evidence.support_explanation: Memory-RL baselines differ in pipeline, not just in the memory component; unmatched comparison.
Search-augmented QA: SkillRL beats EvolveR on 5 of 7 sets (avg 47.1 vs 43.1), with most of the margin from Bamboogle (73.8 vs 54.4).

evidence.quote: maintains competitive performance on OOD tasks like TriviaQA and 2Wiki, confirming that distilled search strategies are task-agnostic.
evidence.support_explanation: Only holdout-like evidence: QA trained on NQ/HotpotQA, evaluated on other datasets; ALFWorld/WebShop have no stated unseen split.

evidence.quote: Validation interval 5 Steps
evidence.support_explanation: Evolution cadence every 5 steps with update threshold 0.4 and capped failures/new skills per evolution; hyperparameters given.

evidence.quote: achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming strong baselines over 15.3% and maintaining robustness as task complexity increases.
evidence.support_explanation: Central performance claim as stated.

evidence.quote: many existing methods still struggle to distinguish high-value experiences from noise or fail to distill core principles that can guide internal decision-making.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated residual of nearest memory-RL neighbors (EvolveR, MemRL); no pinned neighbor text to verify the characterization.

Inference: variants that lack SFT or the library (65.2 / 61.7) fall below plain GRPO (77.6), and no control exists for GRPO with the same o3 cold-start SFT but no skills, so the "attributable to skill augmentation" gain is not isolated from teacher demonstration SFT.

evidence.quote: SFT examples 7,500 (AlfWorld) / 2,400 (WebShop)
evidence.support_explanation: Size of teacher-generated cold-start SFT data (o3); a data advantage not given to GRPO baselines.

signatures.information: base-agent rollouts (successes and failures) distilled by o3; failures rewritten as four-part lessons; at inference the policy sees skills in the prompt; skills for held-out categories absent
signatures.operation: teacher distills strategies from successes and counterfactual lessons from failures; organizes per task category; retrieval top-K (K=6) above a similarity threshold
signatures.output: compact skills claimed 10-20x shorter than raw trajectories (prompt ~10% shorter than raw-memory baseline)
signatures.conditions: stronger teacher available; base policy must be SFT-taught to use skills (cold start)
signatures.feedback: binary task success from the environment; no skill-level utility credit
signatures.selection_rule: no admission test: skills enter if the teacher proposes them; no execution or held-out validation of individual skills
signatures.persistence: library file read by later episodes and all later RL steps; grows 55 -> 100
signatures.claimed_effect: ALFWorld 89.9 vs GRPO 77.6; WebShop success 72.7 vs 66.1; library replaced by raw trajectories -> 61.7/50.2
signatures.failure_boundary: 7B self-distillation fails (42.5/19.6); retrieval noise as library grows; teacher cost

signatures.object: SkillBank edits during RL (validation-failure-triggered recursive evolution)
signatures.information: failed validation trajectories for categories with success below the 0.4 threshold, chosen by diversity-aware round-robin by failure severity; teacher sees current library
signatures.operation: teacher proposes new skills and refinements of ineffective ones; library union new skills; every 5 validation steps
signatures.output: additional or refined skills (capped per evolution)
signatures.selection_rule: teacher judgment only; no accept/reject on measured gain; no rollback
signatures.persistence: library overwritten in place across training; version history not described
signatures.claimed_effect: +5.5 ALFWorld / +2.4 WebShop vs static library; faster convergence (80% by step ~60 vs ~90)
signatures.failure_boundary: validation set both drives evolution and displays the benefit; split for Table 1 unstated

signatures.object: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct weights: teacher-generated cold-start SFT then GRPO on skill-augmented prompts (component_training side)
signatures.information: policy conditions on retrieved skills; o3 traces demonstrate retrieve-interpret-apply
signatures.operation: SFT (7,500 ALFWorld / 2,400 WebShop examples) then GRPO with KL to the SFT reference
signatures.conditions: skills present at train and inference
signatures.failure_boundary: no control of GRPO with o3 SFT and no skills

gap.author_gap: Memory-based agents store raw trajectories (redundant/noisy) and memory-augmented RL methods fail to distill core principles or adapt the policy to use memory.
gap.checked_gap: The raw-vs-distilled contrast is supported inside the authors pipeline (library replaced by raw trajectories 61.7 vs 89.9), so a measurable residual exists. The distinction from the nearest memory-RL neighbors (EvolveR, MemRL), which also distill or co-train, rests on the authors description; neighbor texts are not pinned, so the lineage claim is unverified.
gap.lineage: Reflexion/ExpeL/Mem0/MemP raw or tip memory -> MemRL/EvolveR memory-RL -> hierarchical skill library with validation-driven evolution (SkillRL)
closest_adjacent: EvolveR (jointly updates policy and memory bank)
gap.residue: Self-contained skill abstraction at small scale (7B self-distillation 42.5) and library growth/retrieval noise remain open (authors limitations).
gap.stakes: sample-efficient agentic RL with bounded context
gap.method_response: Teacher-distilled hierarchical skills, SFT cold start, and failure-driven library growth during GRPO.
gap.remaining_gap: Teacher dependence, no pruning/gating of skills, unverified split between evolution data and reported metrics.

claims.selection_vs_test: evolution uses validation failures; table split unstated
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported single-run superiority of the full o3-assisted pipeline; attribution to skill augmentation alone is not isolated.

claims.selection_vs_test: validation set drives evolution and shows the curve
claims.allowed_conclusion: Task-level gain on the selection split; retained-on-held-out not shown.

claims.text: Abstracted hierarchical skills beat raw trajectories.
Skills transfer to search QA and OOD datasets.

claims.text: Experience-based skill discovery works autonomously for sufficiently strong models.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Scoped: only at 1.1T; at 7B self-distilled skills give 42.5.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported: in a pipeline combining o3-distilled hierarchical skills, o3-trace cold-start SFT and GRPO, Qwen2.5-7B reaches 89.9 ALFWorld / 72.7 WebShop success, above reported GRPO and memory-augmented baselines; replacing the library by raw trajectories or removing hierarchy/SFT lowers it; validation-driven evolution adds a few points on the validation split.
not_supported: gain attributable to skill augmentation alone
retained gain on a split disjoint from evolution data (ALFWorld/WebShop)

G.reason: Raw-trajectory noise is a concrete, named bottleneck with an in-paper test (library->raw 61.7 vs 89.9) and named nearest neighbors compared empirically; residual (teacher dependence, library growth) is stated, but neighbor characterization is unverified.

M.reason: The chain distill -> hierarchical retrieval -> SFT-taught use -> RL with failure-triggered edits is reconstructible and yields distinguishable predictions (raw vs distilled, with/without SFT, static vs evolving).

X.reason: Read path, triggers and hyperparameters (interval 5, threshold 0.4, caps) are given, but skill admission has no test, no rollback/version/retirement, the library only grows, and how a skill is judged ineffective is unspecified.

E.measurement.reason: Standard environment success/EM metrics with per-task breakdowns; but baselines are largely replicated from another paper (star) rather than re-run in one protocol, and test split sizes are not given.

E.causality.reason: Informative ablations (raw, hierarchy, SFT, dynamic) and hybrids, but the headline gain is confounded with o3 demonstration SFT and distillation (7B self-distilled 42.5; variants below GRPO) with no GRPO+SFT-without-skills control; baselines are different pipelines.

E.holdout.reason: Evolution is driven by validation failures and its benefit is displayed on the validation set; the split behind Table 1 is not stated. Only the QA transfer to unseen datasets supplies holdout evidence.

E.statistics.reason: Authors answer No for error bars; no seeds, repeats, test denominators or CIs for any table; margins of a few points rest on single runs.

rationale: 技能库分层蒸馏与失败驱动演化链条清楚，库消融有力；但增益与o3教师SFT混杂、演化数据与报告划分不明、无种子/误差线、技能无准入门控。
